concepts.title: Pappachi: Bitter Imperial Entomologist
concepts.definition: Arundhati Roy sketches Reverend E. John Ipe, called Pappachi, a high-ranking entomologist in the imperial service -- proud, aging, and embittered. His grievance is a moth he discovered and named after himself, which science later denied him, reclassifying it as a subspecies of an existing one.
concepts.key_idea: A moth denied, a man defined -- Pappachi's thwarted discovery curdles into lifelong rage.

solution_steps.explain: Pappachi finds a new moth and believes a species will carry his name forever.
Years later science declares it a subspecies -- the recognition, and immortality, are withdrawn.
Denied his moth, he turns his fury inward on his household, beating Mammachi nightly with a brass vase.

concepts.title: Mammachi's Pickles and the Sweet Reversal
concepts.definition: Beside the failed scientist stands Mammachi, Pappachi's wife, who turns her skill into Paradise Pickles and Preserves -- an enterprise that thrives and makes her known. The man denied scientific immortality watches his wife earn the recognition his moth refused him, deepening his envy.
concepts.key_idea: Pickles versus papers -- domestic enterprise outshines scientific ambition, and envy sours further.

solution_steps.explain: Mammachi converts her recipes into a branded business with jars, labels and a growing name.
The wife Pappachi beats gains public recognition precisely as his own name is erased from science.
Roy's quiet gender irony: domestic skill, not imperial science, achieves lasting recognition.

concepts.title: The Moth on the Wall: Symbol of Pappachi's Rage
concepts.definition: After Pappachi's death the moth survives as symbol: his taxidermied specimen sits on Mammachi's wall, and Rahel later imagines Pappachi's Moth as a dark presence in the family's heart, spreading its wings of resentment across generations -- the way denied pride breeds domestic violence.
concepts.key_idea: The moth never dies -- pinned on the wall and unborn in the heart, it outlives its discoverer as a symbol of poisonous pride.

solution_steps.explain: The pinned specimen hangs on Mammachi's wall -- a trophy of failure on display.
Rahel pictures Pappachi's Moth as a dark shape spreading its wings in the chest -- inherited rage.
Roy makes the insect a symbol of how wounded pride propagates itself through a family.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Explain why the reclassification of the moth mattered more to Pappachi than the moth itself.

solution_template.explain: The moth's real damage was never its wings but the denial of Pappachi's immortalisation.
His vanity needed a species bearing his name -- scientific legacy as personal trophy.
Reclassification meant public erasure; his bitterness at that erasure poisons the whole household.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Show how Mammachi's pickle business functions as a quiet reversal of power in the household.

solution_template.explain: Paradise Pickles gives Mammachi income, identity and public praise.
Simultaneously Pappachi loses the scientific name he craved -- a perfect inversion.
The beaten wife becomes the family's real achiever -- Roy's irony against patriarchy.
